title: Control: Add AI / Private Walkthroughs
description: How to choose a safe Control Walkthrough handoff transport for public, private, large, or secret-dependent setup instructions.

steps.title: Use public modules only for permanently public-safe guidance
steps.body: If a walkthrough is generic, reusable, and contains no personal/project-private data, it can live as a normal public Control Walkthrough module. Do not publish something merely because you plan to delete it later: Git history can retain deleted committed content.

steps.title: Private or project-specific one-off: ask for CWZ2
steps.body: For a private/project-specific walkthrough that contains no credentials, ask the AI for a CWZ2 handoff. CWZ2 is gzip-compressed schema-v2 JSON encoded with Base64URL. In Control Walkthrough, open the menu, choose Import guide, paste the one-line CWZ2 code, and press Load.

steps.title: Use CW2 only when gzip decode is unavailable
steps.body: CW2 carries the same schema-v2 JSON as Base64URL without gzip compression. It is larger but is a useful compatibility fallback if the browser cannot decode CWZ2.

steps.title: Large walkthrough: use a local file
steps.body: If a private walkthrough is too long for comfortable copy/paste, have the AI provide a .walkthrough.json file/attachment. Choose Import guide -> Import file and select it from the device. Do not move private content into a public repo just to shorten the paste.

steps.title: Compression is not encryption
steps.body: CWZ2 and CW2 are transport formats, not secrecy. Never place passwords, API keys, bearer tokens, SSH/private keys, recovery codes, cookies, or other credentials in a walkthrough code/file/URL. A walkthrough may generate/capture a value into temporary local memory when needed, but long-lived credentials belong in the provider/server secret store.
steps.humanGate: If an AI asks you to paste a real credential into a public repo or CW code, stop and ask it to keep the value out of the handoff.

steps.title: Private GitHub pointers are best-effort only
steps.body: CWG1 and normal private GitHub blob links can be convenient, but a signed-in GitHub page does not guarantee the userscript can fetch the private raw file. If a private GitHub import returns NetworkError, do not create a PAT just for Control Walkthrough; ask the AI for a CWZ2 code or local walkthrough file instead.

steps.title: What to tell an AI
steps.body: A useful request is: 'I have Control Walkthrough installed. Build a walkthrough for this fix. If it is public-safe, use/update the public module. If it is private/project-specific, give me a CWZ2 code or local file. Never include secrets. Automate safe actions and verify before advancing.'
